clues: This city in the heart of Ontario, in Canada, lies north of Toronto. It is part of a wide gold belt of towns in the south of the land.
Cold air sweeps over warmer lake water from November to January each year. It drops sudden squalls of snow on this town in the snow belt.
Its first town grew up in the War of 1812 as a supply store. British troops on the march drew food and gear from its stores.
In 1985, this town was a hub of a fierce tornado outbreak. The storms struck towns in both Canada and the United States that year.
This town stands on the shore of Kempenfelt Bay. Though a county wraps round it, the town rules itself and makes its own laws.
